name: meeple-as-card-off-v1
description: THE ISOLATION CONTROL FOR R15. Takes the cap and toll changes of the handoff-v2 arm - meepleCapPerColour 2 and slotToll 1 - WITHOUT R15 itself: meepleAsCard stays false, so a meeple can never be spent as a card and only ever buys its colour's action through a neighbour's board, exactly as under v1. This overlay exists because overlays/meeple-as-card-v1.overlay.json changes three knobs at once (R15, the amended cap, the amended toll) and a result from it cannot say which of the three produced it. Running this arm and reading it against BOTH v1 (no knobs set) and the full meeple-as-card-v1 arm turns one three-way confound into two two-way deltas: this-against-v1 isolates what the cap and toll changes do on their own, and meeple-as-card-v1-against-this isolates what R15 adds on top of them. THE PREDICTION IF R15 IS WHERE THE VALUE IS. This arm should read close to v1 on the hook and the meeples-boxed count - a wider cap and a priced slot with nothing new to spend a meeple ON should mostly just let the supply sit deeper rather than circulate faster - and the full arm should be where the game actually changes. THE PREDICTION IF THE CAP AND TOLL ALONE ACCOUNT FOR MOST OF IT. This arm should already read most of the way to the full arm's numbers, and R15 would be doing less work than the design assumes. Read the meeples-spent-as-resources line specifically: under this overlay it should read exactly zero, because there is no resource use to spend a meeple on, which is the sanity check that the isolation actually isolated something. ⚠️ CORRECTED 05/09/2026: the engine reads every one of these knobs now, this arm is a real result, and it no longer reads identically to overlays/meeple-as-card-v1.overlay.json. It is also now pinned against a moved default - Dean ruled R17 in on 05/09/2026, so the shipped game is meepleAsCard true, meepleAsCardGoesTo 'board', slotToll 1 and cap 2 - which is why this overlay's three explicit values matter more than they did when it was written. THE ORIGINAL WARNING, kept because it dates the arm: at that stage of the build the engine did not yet read meepleAsCard or slotToll, so the overlay behaved exactly like the shipped v1 loop at meepleCapPerColour 2.
